title: Release security exceptions and evidence automation
summary: Working workbook for release-security sign-offs that ties RBAC v2 readiness, audit log schema validation, SIEM export mapping, and automated evidence collection. Includes an exception approval template for items that cannot meet gate criteria before launch.
content:
Purpose:
This working document is intended to be used by release engineers, security owners, and product leads to:
- Validate that a release meets the security gate for RBAC v2 rollout, audit logging, SIEM forwarding, and evidence automation.
- Provide a lightweight exception approval workflow when technical constraints prevent full compliance prior to launch.
- Capture the automated evidence collection steps and sample queries used by the security audit runbook.

Scope:
Applies to any public or Dedicated/Private deployment release that includes changes to access control, authentication paths, logging pipelines, or telemetry exports (SIEM). Not intended for purely client-side UI tweaks unless they change auth/permission behavior.

Quick checklist (use before final sign-off):
- RBAC v2: role-schema changes audited and migration plan attached (link to migration playbook).
- RBAC tests: unit + integration tests pass; authz smoke runs in staging; policy samples for common roles attached.
- Audit logs: event schema version bumped to v2.1; mandatory fields present: timestamp_ms, request_id, actor_id, actor_role, resource_type, resource_id, action, outcome, ip, user_agent, kv_cache_key (if applicable).
- SIEM export: mapping manifest created, indices validated in SIEM staging, transport secured (TLS mTLS pair) and credentials rotated.
- Evidence automation: nightly evidence collection script executed against staging and archived artifacts uploaded to evidence-bucket with retention tag.
- Exception approvals: any failing item must have an exception ticket with compensating controls and explicit approver.

RBAC v2 readiness notes:
- Migration approach: shadow policy evaluation for 48hrs in staging followed by staged rollout to 10% production traffic.
- Known gap: legacy service-account tokens still include role "svc-legacy-admin" that is not mapped in RBAC v2. Mitigation: token-life reduction and scope filter applied at gateway. See JIRA SEC-4789.
- Required artifacts for gate: policy diff file, test matrix, rollout canary config, and rollback playbook.

Audit log schema (summary):
- Version: v2.1 (increment for RBAC additions).
- Core fields (required): [timestamp_ms, request_id, trace_id, actor_type, actor_id, actor_role, resource_type, resource_id, action, action_category, outcome, latency_ms, http_status, ip, user_agent, service_name, env, region, request_size, response_size, kv_cache_key].
- Optional fields: feature_flag_state, sample_output_hash, model_version, quantization_profile.
- Notes: actor_role should be the evaluated role after RBAC v2 resolution (not the legacy role claim). This is important for downstream SIEM rules and alerts.

Sample SIEM export mapping (examples for common fields):
- SIEM Index: redwood-audit-{env}\n- timestamp_ms -> @timestamp (convert ms -> ISO8601)
- request_id -> event.id
- actor_id -> user.id
- actor_role -> user.role_resolved
- action -> event.action
- resource_type/resource_id -> object.type / object.id
- outcome -> event.outcome (allowed|denied|error)
- kv_cache_key -> labels.kv_cache_key
- model_version -> labels.model_version

Transport/security for SIEM: ensure TLS 1.3 and mTLS where supported. Broker credentials stored in HashiCorp Vault and rotated on a 30-day cadence. Run a smoke test post-deploy: curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://siem-ingest.staging.redwood/health

Evidence automation runbook (high level):
1) Trigger: scheduled nightly run in CI for the release branch and manually after major changes.
2) Steps:
   - Run policy-coverage tool to produce JSON reports for RBAC evaluation.
   - Run audit-log-schema-validator against sample audit events (scripts/schema-validator.py).
   - Push exported logs (limited window) to SIEM staging index for mapping/dev team to verify.
   - Collect artifacts: policy-diff.txt, unit-test-summary.txt, schema-validator-report.json, siem-mapping-sanity.txt, canary-metrics.csv.
   - Bundle artifacts and upload to s3://redwood-evidence/releases/<release-tag>/evidence-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz with sha256 checksum file.
3) Verifications: automated checksum + size validation; retention tag set to 365d; notify security channel with secure link.

Automated queries & sanity checks (examples):
- RBAC shadow evaluation anomalies: count of requests where actor_role is null but actor_id present -> should be 0.
  ELK query: event.action: * AND NOT user.role_resolved: * AND event.outcome: *
- Unexpected high-deny spike: compare denies in last 5m vs rolling 24h baseline (threshold 5x).
- SIEM index health: document count in last 24h > expected_min_count (per service).

Exception approval template (use if any gate fails):
- Exception ID: (auto JIRA)
- Component: (e.g., RBAC, AuditLogs, SIEMExport)
- Short description of gap: plain language summary.
- Risk assessment: low|medium|high and brief rationale.
- Compensating controls in place: (e.g., increased monitoring, temporary deny-by-default rules, manual audit cadence).
- Proposed mitigation timeline: ETA and milestones.
- Owner(s): name and pager/Slack handle.
- Required approvers: security-engineering lead, product manager, release manager.
- Approvals: space for approver name and date.
- Link to evidence artifacts: (s3/Confluence/JIRA).

Sign-off matrix (for final release):
- Security engineering: name, signature, date
- Platform SRE: name, signature, date
- Product owner: name, signature, date
- Release manager: name, signature, date

Open questions / TODOs (working items):
- Confirm that SIEM staging will accept kv_cache_key (sensitive?) — privacy review pending (Evelyn).
- Decide whether to include model_version in public audit exports (privacy + PII review).
- Automate exception creation from failed gate to produce JIRA with pre-filled fields.

Quick references / links inside doc:
- RBAC v2 design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SSEC/RBAC+v2+Design
- Schema validator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/main/tools/schema-validator
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/releases/
- SIEM runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SSEC/SIEM+Integration+Runbook

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally a practical workbook rather than a prescriptive policy doc. Expect to iterate after a couple of release cycles; please leave line comments and at least one concrete follow-up task if you object to any mitigation.
- If you are approving an exception, please add the compensating controls subsection in the Jira ticket and assign Evelyn and Marco for verification.
